world.headline: US-Iran 60-day understanding expires without a deal as Trump threatens to bomb Oman
world.body: The memorandum of understanding the United States and Iran signed on 17 June lapsed on Monday with no wider peace agreement and the war now in its 24th week. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei ruled out any extension, saying the 60-day clock was irrelevant because Washington had violated the understanding from the start. Trump told Fox News the US would bomb Oman if it got in the way of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, days after Tehran said it had reached its own understanding with Muscat on future shipping arrangements.

world.headline: Brent settles at $90.87 as Hormuz traffic falls to three ships in a day
world.body: Brent crude gained 2.7% on Monday to settle at $90.87 a barrel after Iran ruled out extending the interim deal and warned it could escalate. Kpler data showed just three vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday against a five-day average of twelve. Roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas normally moves through the waterway, and the near-shutdown is now the main channel through which the conflict is reaching global fuel and food prices.

world.headline: Trump orders US participation in South Korea drills cut hours before they began
world.body: Trump directed the Pentagon to substantially reduce American involvement in the 11-day Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise less than a day before it started, calling the drills a hostile signal to a North Korea he described as unthreatening. He linked the decision to his relationship with Kim Jong Un and to President Lee Jae Myung's refusal to help against Iran. Seoul's Joint Chiefs said the exercise began on Monday as planned.

world.headline: Russia strikes Danube port after one of Ukraine's largest aerial attacks of the war
world.body: Russia hit port infrastructure in the Odesa region on Monday in response to a weekend Ukrainian assault that Moscow said involved a record 1,478 drones shot down in 24 hours, with at least six people killed. Kyiv's targets included a Wildberries logistics hub near Moscow, part of a shift towards Russian economic infrastructure rather than purely military sites. Russia sent 128 drones into Ukraine overnight on 17 August.

world.headline: Russian court jails Yabloko's Lev Shlosberg for 11 years over anti-war posts
world.body: A court in Pskov sentenced the liberal Yabloko party's deputy chairman to 11 years and one month in a penal colony on Monday for spreading false information about and discrediting the military, over a 2022 newspaper front page he shared and a video calling for a ceasefire. Shlosberg told the court he was the victim of a political trial. Separately, Russia's Supreme Court upheld its decision to bar Yabloko from the 18-20 September parliamentary vote.

world.headline: Nvidia backs $105 billion in financing for OpenAI's Ohio data centre
world.body: A securities filing disclosed that Nvidia will guarantee up to $105 billion in credit for an OpenAI campus in southern Ohio being developed by SoftBank subsidiary SB Energy. The facility is designed for an initial 4.25 gigawatts with an option for a further 3.75 gigawatts, phasing in from 2028. The figure is well below the $250 billion earlier under discussion, cut after investors questioned Nvidia's exposure to circular financing arrangements with its own customers.

world.headline: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak becomes the deadliest in the country's history
world.body: The Bundibugyo virus outbreak declared on 15 May has now killed 2,325 people out of 4,945 confirmed cases as of 15 August, passing the 2,299 deaths of the 2018-20 epidemic. The case fatality rate has risen to 46%, with 730 patients in isolation and 1,040 recoveries. The UN describes it as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, with many patients dying before reaching a clinic.

world.headline: Caltech brings fibre-optic loss levels to silicon chips at visible wavelengths
world.body: Writing in Nature, a Caltech team reported germano-silicate waveguides made with standard semiconductor lithography and surface reflow that cut optical loss up to twentyfold against silicon nitride at visible wavelengths and improved laser coherence more than a hundredfold. The waveguides are laid out in spirals to extend path length in a small footprint. The likely applications are optical clocks, miniature atomic sensors, quantum systems and lower-power data centre interconnects.

world.headline: New York factory activity hits a multi-year high as September Fed cut odds slip to 33%
world.body: The New York Fed's August manufacturing survey reached a multi-year high, driven by a jump in unfilled orders, while the two-year Treasury yield eased to 4.1542%. Futures pricing on Monday afternoon implied about a 32.6% chance of a cut at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting, down from earlier in the month. The Fed left rates at 3.5%-3.75% in July and has no August meeting.

world.headline: Champions League play-off first legs begin with 14 clubs chasing the league phase
world.body: The 2026-27 Champions League play-off round opens on 18-19 August with second legs on 25-26 August, deciding the last places in the league phase. Ties include Celtic against LASK and Fenerbahce or Sturm Graz against Sparta Prague or Lyon. Losing sides drop into the Europa League league phase; the main draw follows on 27 August.

india.headline: Seven women killed in stampede at Bihar's Ashok Dham temple during Shravan rush
india.body: The crush happened early on Monday at the Lakhisarai temple on the third Somwari of Shravan, after two trains arrived between 6.30 and 6.45 am and a rumour spread that a live wire had fallen. An electric pole carrying a cable did collapse beside the men's queue, and the panic pushed the adjacent women's line over. All seven dead were women; the state announced Rs 4 lakh for each family, with Rs 2 lakh more from the PM's relief fund.

india.headline: Hotel fire near Tarapith temple in Birbhum kills at least seven pilgrims
india.body: Fire broke out around 4 am on Monday on the ground floor of a four-storey hotel at Tarapith in West Bengal's Birbhum district, apparently from an air-conditioning unit, and spread through the building. At least seven died, with several reports putting the toll at eight including five people from Meghalaya. Twenty-two guests were brought out by ladder and eleven were taken to hospital; the district SP said no smoke or flames were visible from outside.

india.headline: Assam flood toll reaches 103 as the affected population falls to about 87,000
india.body: The death toll from this monsoon's Brahmaputra flooding has risen to 103, up from 100 on 10 August, though the number of people still affected has dropped to roughly 87,000 from a peak of about 1.1 million across 25 districts. Golaghat, Nagaon and Sivasagar remain the worst hit. The IMD has forecast widespread rain across the state through 18 August, and Assam is running a door-to-door damage assessment due to finish by 31 August.

india.headline: Supreme Court halts Allahabad High Court proceedings against Rahul Gandhi
india.body: A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant asked the Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court not to proceed with a disproportionate assets complaint against the Leader of the Opposition, and barred the CBI and ED from filing any report under the high court's earlier directions. The complaint was brought by a Karnataka BJP worker. Kapil Sibal appeared for Gandhi and ASG S V Raju for the CBI; proceedings stand deferred until further orders.

india.headline: Telangana publishes SIR draft rolls with 2.65 crore electors and notices for 5.82 lakh
india.body: The Election Commission released draft electoral rolls for all 119 assembly constituencies in Telangana on Monday after the special intensive revision enumeration closed, with 2.65 crore electors having filed forms. Claims and objections run from 17 August to 16 September. In Hyderabad district alone, 5.82 lakh electors, about 20.8% of digitised forms, will be served notices because their details could not be matched to the 2002 rolls.

india.headline: Nifty falls for a fifth straight session as crude nears $90 and the rupee slips
india.body: The Sensex closed down 281.09 points at 77,728.16 on Monday and the Nifty fell 78.35 points to 24,287.65, a fifth consecutive decline. IT, FMCG and telecom shares led the selling, while metals bucked the trend and the midcap and smallcap indices ended higher. The rupee weakened about 17 paise to around 95.59 a dollar in early trade as the West Asia conflict kept oil elevated.

india.headline: Retail inflation rises to a 19-month high of 4.45% in July on food and services
india.body: CPI inflation edged up from 4.38% in June, the highest since December 2024 and a second straight month above the RBI's 4% target. Food inflation rose to 5.52% from 5.32%, with restaurant and personal care prices also contributing. Rural inflation at 4.84% again ran well ahead of the urban rate of 3.96%. The RBI held the repo rate at 5.25% on 5 August while raising its FY27 growth forecast to 6.7%.

india.headline: IISc releases SraVaani, a speech recognition model covering 65 Indian languages
india.body: The SPIRE Lab at IISc, with ARTPARK and support from Google, has open-sourced the first Indian multilingual speech recognition model trained across 20 scheduled and 45 regional languages and dialects, more than 40 of which no existing system officially supports. It was built on the FastConformer architecture using over 31,000 hours of Indian speech and is on Hugging Face under an MIT licence. Coverage includes Garo, Kokborok, Tulu, Bundeli, Gondi and Wancho.

india.headline: Ayush Shetty knocks out world number one Shi Yuqi on day one of the badminton worlds in Delhi
india.body: The 21-year-old, ranked 22nd, beat the defending champion 21-14, 13-21, 21-19 on his World Championships debut at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium. All five Indians in action on Monday won: P V Sindhu beat Ireland's Sophia Noble 21-7, 21-11, and both women's doubles pairs advanced. Delhi is hosting the championships for the first time since 2009; they run to 23 August.

india.headline: Suthar and Jadeja take seven as India build a 178-run lead in the Galle Test
india.body: Sri Lanka were bowled out for 284 in 79.4 overs on day three, with Manav Suthar and Ravindra Jadeja sharing seven wickets despite a century from Dinusha. That followed India's first innings built around Devdutt Padikkal's 167. India lead by 178 with two days left, and the Galle forecast points to cloud and around a 40% chance of rain on day four.
